title: Design System: The AI-Native Marketing Handbook

display-lg.purpose: Secondary large headlines, one step down from Display.

label.purpose: Mono kickers, rail labels, D-numbers, provenance chips.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The single authored easing curve for every entrance/transition in the system.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Cut-corner CTA button — the sites one signature shape, reserved for primary calls to action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; border-radius: 12px 12px 12px 0; padding: 0 24px; background: #C2410C; color: #F7F5F1; font-family: "Bricolage Grotesque", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.3125rem; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #9A3412; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C2410C; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Inline Text Link
components.description: The sites secondary/ghost button role — a plain underlined ember-deep link, no button chrome.
components.css: .ds-link { color: #9A3412; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: rgba(154,52,18,0.7); text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 0.15em; transition: text-decoration-color 0.2s; } .ds-link:hover { text-decoration-color: #9A3412; }

components.name: Prerequisite Chip
components.description: Small pill-shaped nav chip, used for read-first prerequisite links and provenance marks.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid #DDD8CE; background: #F7F5F1; padding: 4px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #3A3630; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #9A3412; color: #9A3412; }

components.name: Key Callout Card
components.description: Tinted callout card for a key/caution highlight — one of the systems only tinted surfaces.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-callout { border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid #DDD8CE; background: rgba(194,65,12,0.05); padding: 20px; } .ds-callout-label { font-family: "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.22em; color: #9A3412; } .ds-callout-title { margin-top: 4px; font-weight: 500; color: #14120F; } .ds-callout-body { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 0.92rem; line-height: 1.6; color: #3A3630; }

components.name: Decorative Swoosh Background
components.description: Full-bleed 4%-opacity ember bezier curve behind page-hero content — the sites one piece of pure-geometry decoration.
components.css: .ds-swoosh { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: -56px; z-index: -10; height: 600px; width: 100vw; transform: translateX(-50%); overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; }

narrative.overview: This is a working reference document, not a marketing site pretending to teach — the visual language of a well-kept field notebook: warm paper, hairline rules, mono-set labels standing in for margin notes, and exactly two colors of ink used on purpose. Ember marks consequence; pine marks construction. Neither is decoration; hierarchy comes from type weight, spacing, and hairline rules first, color only when something specifically needs it. The system is flat by design — no shadows, no gradients, no glass. One custom shape carries the whole personality: a rounded rectangle with one corner squared off, used only on primary calls-to-action.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, near-white paper background — never pure white, never dark mode
Two rationed accent hues (burnt ember, ledger pine), each with a fixed semantic job
Bricolage Grotesque display type paired with Switzer body copy and Geist Mono for every label/kicker/rail
Flat surfaces, hairline rule borders, zero shadows
One signature cut-corner shape, reserved for primary CTAs only
Decorative background curves (swooshes) at 4% ember opacity — texture, never a competing color

rules.name: The One-Job Rule
rules.body: Ember means consequence, pine means construction. A color never gets reused for its other meaning just because a screen needs another accent.

rules.name: The Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: Ember and pine are never the sole difference between two things a reader has to tell apart. Always pair color with position, an icon, or a text label.

rules.name: The Mono-Meta Rule
rules.body: Anything that is metadata about the content renders in Geist Mono, uppercase, wide-tracked. Anything that is the content renders in Bricolage Grotesque or Switzer.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere. If something needs to feel lifted, give it a surface fill and a rule border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The One-Cut Rule
rules.body: The asymmetric cut-corner shape appears on primary CTAs only. The moment it shows up on a second component type, it stops meaning click this and starts meaning nothing.

dos: Do keep ember and pine rare — most components use neither; color is the exception, not the default source of hierarchy.
Do pair every color-coded distinction with an icon, label, or position, never color alone.
Do use ember-deep/pine-deep, not the base hue, for any small-size text.
Do render every kicker, rail label, D-number, and meta tag in mono, uppercase, wide-tracked.
Do use the cut-corner shape only on primary CTA buttons.
Do keep decorative background curves at ~4% opacity, single-hue, geometry only.
donts: Dont add a shadow anywhere. The system is flat; a shadow breaks the paper metaphor.
Dont use pine as inline prose text or a link color — thats ember-deeps job.
Dont introduce a second signature shape. The cut corner means click this; a second irregular shape dilutes it.
Dont go dark mode. color-scheme: light is set explicitly at root; this is a light-only system.
Dont use pure white or pure black — paper/ink are both warm-tinted.
